name: Artist's Talent
description:
Whenever you cast a noncreature spell, draw a card.

{2}{R}: Level 2

{2}{R}: Level 3
assumptions: Rendered nodes E and F (each an activated `becomes` on `self` with `cost:{2}{R}` and `cond:class_level=2`/`=3`) using the standard Class-enchantment level-up line format ("{cost}: Level N") rather than a prose sentence — this is the direct, non-inventive reading of "pay this cost, this permanent becomes class level N" for this exact node shape.

Ordered the three printed ability lines as base ability (C/D) → Level 2 (E) → Level 3 (F), matching how Class cards conventionally lay out level tiers, since the flow graph doesn't otherwise fix a display order among independent roots.
couldNotDerive: The standard Class reminder text ("Gain the next level as a sorcery to add its ability.") — no node or flag encodes it, so it's omitted rather than assumed.
Any abilities unlocked specifically at class level 2 or level 3 beyond simply reaching that level — nothing flows downstream from E or F describing further effects.
The card's name (withheld by design), supertype, and rarity — none are present in the self registry or nodes.
notes:
Real card confirmed via forge-model/data/artist-s-talent.txt: Artist's Talent, {1}{R} Enchantment — Class — "(Gain the next level as a sorcery to add its ability.) Whenever you cast a noncreature spell, you may discard a card. If you do, draw a card. {2}{R}: Level 2 -- Noncreature spells you cast cost {1} less to cast. {2}{R}: Level 3 -- If a source you control would deal noncombat damage to an opponent or a permanent an opponent controls, it deals that much damage plus 2 instead." Mana cost, type line, and the base-ability trigger condition (cast a noncreature spell) all check out. Two real decomposition/translation gaps, both traced to specific Forge fields with no corresponding handling in app/lib/forgeTranslate.ts (not a schema gap — SCHEMA.md's existing `move`+`may` idiom and `modifier`/replacement-fact conventions could express all three missing pieces if the translator built the nodes):

1. Node D (`emit draw`, downstream of trigger C) drops the card's actual cost entirely. The real ability is `SVar:TrigDiscard:AB$ Draw | Cost$ Discard<1/Card>` — "you may discard a card. If you do, draw a card," i.e. the draw is gated behind an optional discard cost. forgeTranslate.ts's lineType-'A' cost handling (~line 942, `if (row.lineType === 'A' && fields.Cost && !/^Sac</.test(fields.Cost))`) only special-cases `Sac<...>` (checked earlier via regex at line 889) and a bare `T` tap token (line 944); a `Discard<1/Card>` cost token matches neither branch, so it falls through to `translateOwnEffect` with no cost node built at all (the code's own comment at ~935-941 flags exactly this shape — "A pure mana-only cost (no T) has no such node... left as a smaller, separate open gap" — Discard<> hits the identical gap). Net effect: D has no upstream `move` node (hand->gy, thing:self-chosen card, flags `may`) representing the discard, and no `may` flag of its own, so both this examiner and any real consumer reconstruct the ability as an unconditional "draw a card" rather than the real optional discard-to-draw exchange. Confirmed correctly flagged by neither examiner list since the missing input gave no hint anything was gated — this is a decomposition gap, not agent misinterpretation.

2. Nodes E and F (the level-2/3 `becomes` nodes) carry zero information about what either level actually grants, and the examiner correctly reported this as "could not derive." The real script is `K:Class:2:2 R:AddStaticAbility$ SReduceCost` (SVar SReduceCost: `Mode$ ReduceCost | ValidCard$ Card.nonCreature | Type$ Spell | Activator$ You | Amount$ 1 | Secondary$ True` — "noncreature spells you cast cost {1} less") and `K:Class:3:2 R:AddReplacementEffect$ DoubleDamage` (SVar DoubleDamage: `Event$ DamageDone | ValidSource$ Card.YouCtrl,Emblem.YouCtrl | ValidTarget$ Permanent.OppCtrl,Opponent | IsCombat$ False | ReplaceWith$ DmgPlus2`, chaining to SVar DmgPlus2/X's `ReplaceCount$DamageAmount/Plus.2` — "noncombat damage to an opponent or their permanent is dealt plus 2 instead"). forgeScript.ts's parser does correctly chase both `AddStaticAbility$` and `AddReplacementEffect$` into child 'S' rows under the ClassLevel node (per forgeScript.ts's own AddStaticAbility$/AddReplacementEffect$ handling), and forgeTranslate.ts's `ek === 'ClassLevel'` branch (line ~1507-1521) does recurse into `tree.children` after building the `becomes` node. But translateEffectRow's static-ability branch (~line 780-863) has no case for `Mode$ ReduceCost` nor for an `Event$ DamageDone` + `ReplaceWith$` replacement effect — both fall through to the generic `if (!handled) { ctx.unmapped.push(...) }` catch-all (line 849-860), which only logs a label for developer visibility and never calls `addNode`/`attach`. So neither ability produces any node, and nothing gets wired into `flow.steps['E']` or `flow.steps['F']` — the level-up nodes are dead ends in the graph with no way to tell a reconstructor what either level does. This is the single biggest gap on this card and is a straightforward decomposition/translator gap: SReduceCost could map to a `modifier` node (e.g. `cond:cost_reduction=amount=1;type=noncreature_spell`) and DoubleDamage to a `modifier`/replacement-fact node (e.g. `cond:dmg_replace=plus2;noncombat;vs=opponent`), each attached as a child of the corresponding `becomes` node, the same way PutCounter/Pump's `cond:delta=` idiom already works.
